base_source: TTM through Q2 FY2026 from EDGAR 10-Q YTD: OCF $7,311M - $3,688M + $3,085M = $6,708M; capex $3,855M - $1,968M + $2,437M = $4,324M; SBC $157M - $83M + $101M = $175M; OE TTM $2,209M / 612M H1 FY2026 diluted shares = $3.61. Latest FY $5.04 rejected as distorted (decade-high OCF in the $2.5B Ocado impairment year; maintenance OE only $3.15/sh and falling); 3-yr median $3.74 is close to the TTM and gives the same Tier D.
moat_justification: Local #1/#2 market density, procurement/logistics scale, Our Brands private label, loyalty data feeding Kroger Precision Marketing (profit +24% in Q2 FY2026), and pharmacy/fuel frequency — against zero consumer switching costs and Walmart's larger price leadership, Costco/Aldi/Amazon pressure (identical sales +0.2% in Q2, FY guidance cut to +0.2-0.8%), 1-3% margins, the blocked Albertsons merger that denied the scale step-change, and the failed Ocado automation bet ($2.5B impairment, pivot to third-party fulfillment).
name: The Kroger Co.
one_liner: Durable defensive grocer with only a weak 4/10 moat (local scale and retail media vs Walmart's price leadership and zero switching costs) — at $62.56 (17.3x TTM owner's earnings, net debt 5.3x OE) the weighted IRR is just 8.8% with IV@15% of $31.04, even the super-bull case (13.2%) fails to clear 15%, and it clears the hurdle only at ~$31, or ~$23 with a margin of safety.
